lab.title: Access Modifiers and API Boundaries
lab.objective: Observe access modifiers from callers inside and outside an assembly.
lab.task: A library exposes a public document service while hiding its internal formatter implementation.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/optional/access-boundaries from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/11: Create the isolated folder exercises/optional/access-boundaries. Do not add its projects to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/11: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: A library exposes a public document service while hiding its internal formatter implementation.
Step 3/11: Create isolated DocumentLibrary and Runner console/class-library projects and reference DocumentLibrary from Runner.
Step 4/11: In DocumentLibrary, add public DocumentService with public Publish and public LastTitle with a private setter.
Step 5/11: Inside DocumentService, add private Normalize because callers do not need that implementation detail.
Step 6/11: Add protected virtual FormatLabel so a derived document service can customize the label.
Step 7/11: Add sealed BrandedDocumentService and override the protected member.
Step 8/11: Add internal sealed InternalDocumentFormatter and confirm Runner cannot name it across the assembly boundary.
Step 9/11: In Runner, call only the public members, build both projects, and run the result.
Step 10/11: Build with dotnet build exercises/optional/access-boundaries --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 11/11: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/optional/access-boundaries --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.

reveals.text: Complete isolated solution. Keep it in this module folder only.
